stages.title: CITIZENSHIP AS LEGAL MEMBERSHIP: CITIZEN, ALIEN AND THE CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS MAP
stages.terms: India's rights map follows constitutional text, not a citizen-versus-alien slogan: Articles 14, 20, 21 and 25 protect persons; Articles 15, 16, 19 and 29 are citizen-specific; Article 30 speaks of minorities; and voting is statutory, not a Fundamental Right.
stages.mechanism: Naturalised and registered citizens are not constitutionally excluded merely because their citizenship was acquired after birth.
stages.consequence: India's rights map follows constitutional text, not a citizen-versus-alien slogan: Articles 14, 20, 21 and 25 protect persons; Articles 15, 16, 19 and 29 are citizen-specific; Article 30 speaks of minorities; and voting is statutory, not a Fundamental Right.
stages.trap: "Only citizens possess fundamental rights." Wrong. Some rights are citizen-specific; many crucial protections, especially Articles 14 and 21, protect persons.
stages.answer: Citizenship is the legally recognised membership of the Indian political community: it links allegiance and protection, allocates political voice and selected public offices, and remains principally statutory after the Constitution's commencement settlement.

stages.title: CITIZENSHIP, DOMICILE AND RESIDENCE - AND WHY INDIA STILL HAS SINGLE CITIZENSHIP
stages.terms: India combines one national citizenship and one Indian domicile with constitutionally authorised regional protection; residence preferences, Articles 16(3), 19(5) and 371 safeguards do not create State citizenship.
stages.mechanism: Single citizenship serves integration and equal political membership, but it does not produce identical residence benefits everywhere.
stages.consequence: The expression "State domicile" is often used administratively, but it usually describes residence/local-status rules, not a sovereign domicile or separate citizenship.
stages.trap: Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination on place of birth, but does not list residence as a prohibited ground; residence preferences remain subject to Article 14 and the rest of the Constitution.
stages.answer: India combines one national citizenship and one Indian domicile with constitutionally authorised regional protection; residence preferences, Articles 16(3), 19(5) and 371 safeguards do not create State citizenship.

stages.title: ARTICLE 8 - PERSONS OF INDIAN ORIGIN ORDINARILY RESIDENT OUTSIDE INDIA
stages.terms: Article 8 covers a person ordinarily residing outside India if that person, or either parent or any grandparent, was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935, and the person was registered as an Indian citizen by an Indian diplomatic or consular representative.

stages.title: ARTICLE 9 - THE COMMENCEMENT-CONTEXT FOREIGN-CITIZENSHIP DISQUALIFIER
stages.terms: Article 9 says that no person shall be a citizen of India by virtue of Article 5, or be deemed a citizen under Article 6 or Article 8, if the person has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State.

stages.title: ARTICLE 10 - CONTINUANCE SUBJECT TO PARLIAMENTARY LAW

stages.title: ARTICLE 11 - PARLIAMENT'S CITIZENSHIP POWER
stages.terms: Article 11 declares that the preceding provisions do not detract from Parliament's power to make law concerning acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other citizenship matters.
stages.mechanism: Citizenship is therefore a constitutional status predominantly regulated by statute; it is not itself enumerated as a Fundamental Right.
stages.consequence: That does not make citizenship decisions immune from Articles 14, 21 or judicial review.

stages.title: CITIZENSHIP ACT, 1955 - THE STATUTORY ARCHITECTURE
stages.terms: The Citizenship Act, 1955 creates five acquisition routes—birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory—and three distinct loss routes—renunciation, termination and category-limited deprivation—each with its own trigger and safeguards.

stages.title: ASSAM ACCORD, SECTION 6A AND THE NRC CUT-OFF
stages.terms: Section 6A was inserted by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985 to implement the citizenship component of the Assam Accord.

stages.answer: Section 6A is an Assam-specific route to Indian citizenship: pre-1966 entrants are deemed citizens, the 1966–before-25-March-1971 stream faces detection, registration and ten years without electoral-roll inclusion, and post-cut-off entrants receive no protection.

stages.title: OCI AND PIO EVOLUTION - DIASPORA CONNECTION WITHOUT CITIZENSHIP
stages.terms: A person who, or whose parent/grandparent/great-grandparent, is or was a citizen of Pakistan or Bangladesh, or another country notified by the Central Government, is excluded from ordinary Section 7A eligibility.

stages.answer: OCI is calibrated diaspora access for a foreign national—not dual citizenship—because notified mobility and socio-economic facilities coexist with no vote, no Indian passport and no claim to citizen-reserved public office.

stages.title: CAA, ARTICLE 14, SECULARISM AND ASSAM - ARGUMENT TREE, NOT SLOGAN
stages.terms: Because secularism is a basic feature, critics argue that a religion-coded citizenship preference must receive exacting constitutional scrutiny.
